reason: The transporter-bearing cell provides a route for the arriving fuel to enter.
expectation: Glucose and oxygen will become available inside the cell for energy production.

effect: The cell first becomes a muscle fibre scaffold; the fuel combination I tried was not available.
reaction: I was surprised the cell combined with the fibre structures before taking in fuel.
reason: Thin actin filaments and thick myosin filaments are the parts that interact to produce a muscle pull.
expectation: They will form a contractile arrangement for the muscle fibre.

effect: The thin and thick filaments formed sliding filament units, which appear ready to fit into the muscle fibre.
reaction: The overlapping arrangement makes the next construction step clear.
reason: The fibre scaffold has spaces for contractile units, and the sliding filament units match that role.
expectation: The sliding filament units will be installed in the muscle fibre.

effect: The sliding filament units are now installed in the muscle fibre; it still needs energy and signals to pull and relax.
reaction: The packed fibre makes the construction progress clear.
reason: Mitochondria use fuel and oxygen in the process that supplies usable energy.
expectation: This will advance energy production for the muscle fibre.

effect: Glucose and oxygen produced fuelled mitochondria, with glucose first split in the cell fluid.
reaction: The picture clarifies that fuel processing begins outside the mitochondrion.
reason: ADP and phosphate are the remaining ingredients for making ATP from the energy supplied by the fuelled mitochondria.
expectation: The mitochondria will produce ATP for the muscle fibre.

effect: The fuelled mitochondria produced an ATP supply, and the result shows ADP and phosphate returning for ATP to be remade.
reaction: The cycle makes the continuing energy supply clearer.
reason: The filament-filled fibre needs ATP for its pulling machinery.
expectation: The ATP supply will prepare the fibre's filaments to pull.

effect: The ATP supply prepared the fibre's myosin heads to reset, while the thin filament binding sites remain covered.
reaction: The close-up makes ATP's role more specific, though the fibre is not pulling yet.
reason: The calcium signal reaches the filaments and may expose the binding sites needed for a pull.
expectation: Calcium will enable the prepared filaments to interact and the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites, allowing the filaments to slide and the fibre to shorten. The remaining goal is relaxation.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments sliding is clear and useful.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes can return calcium to storage so the fibre can relax.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage, allowing the muscle fibre to relax.

effect: The calcium pumps returned calcium to storage using ATP, covering the grip sites and stopping the pull. The fibre relaxed under an outside pull and the goal is complete.
reaction: I found it useful that relaxation also requires cellular work.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the fibre shorten was most worthwhile: the description connected calcium, exposed grip sites and myosin pulling, while distinguishing sliding filaments from a shortening fibre.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the sliding filament units was straightforward, but its result added less explanation than the later close-ups.

surprise.text: I was surprised that relaxation uses ATP to pump calcium back into storage.

arbitrary.text: My first fuel combination was unavailable, and the cell instead combined automatically with the muscle fibre structures. The scaffold made sense afterward, but the required order was not clear beforehand.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: assembling the fibre and then seeing how ATP and calcium change its behavior made me curious about how it connects to larger body systems.
